hero.headline: US strikes Iran military site as Tehran reports attack on American base
hero.body:
The United States military has assembled sufficient forces in the Middle East to launch strikes against Iran as soon as this weekend, according to multiple news outlets citing unnamed sources. However, President Trump has not yet made a final decision on whether to proceed with an attack.

Trump has repeatedly demanded that Iran cease its nuclear program and has warned he intends to use force if no agreement is reached. The New York Times, CBS News and CNN all reported that the US military has positioned enough air and naval resources in the region to carry out strikes in the coming days. Reuters reported a slightly different timeline, noting that top US national security advisers were told during a Wednesday White House meeting that all deployed forces should be in place by mid-March.

Iran is expected to submit a written proposal addressing its standoff with the US following talks held in Geneva on Tuesday. White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said during a Wednesday press conference that "Iran would be very wise to make a deal with President Trump." She acknowledged "a little bit of progress" from the Geneva talks but stressed that the two sides remain "very far apart on some issues."

Trump met Wednesday with Steve Witkoff, a real estate developer serving as an envoy, and Jared Kushner, his son-in-law, who are leading indirect talks with Iran. According to journalist Barak Ravid reporting on Israeli television, US sources described the Geneva talks with Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi as a "nothingburger" and indicated the Pentagon was preparing for a joint Israeli-US offensive that could last weeks.

The military buildup is substantial. The USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier group is already deployed in the region, while the USS Gerald Ford is en route to the Middle East. The Pentagon has also positioned dozens of refueling tankers and more than 50 additional fighter jets in the region. At the same time, CBS News reported that the Pentagon is moving some personnel out of the Middle East to minimize potential casualties from Iranian counterattacks.

Israel is also preparing for the possibility of joining strikes with the US, according to the New York Times.

Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov warned against military action, telling Saudi Arabia's Al-Arabiya television that "the consequences are not good" of any new US strike on Iran. "No one wants an increase in tension. Everyone understands this is playing with fire," Lavrov said, calling on the US to allow Iran to pursue a peaceful nuclear program.

In June, the US struck key nuclear enrichment sites in Iran, while Israeli fighter jets struck dozens of targets across the country, including a long-range missile site in Yazd.

cards.headline: Internet restored in Iran after monthslong shutdown, with restrictions
cards.body:
Iranians have regained internet access following authorities' decision to end a monthslong shutdown. However, connectivity remains inconsistent, with slow and spotty service reported in some areas.

Major social media and video platforms face significant restrictions. YouTube and Instagram are among the apps heavily limited for users attempting to access them.

cards.headline: Ukrainian President Zelensky asks Trump and Congress for Patriot missile interceptors
cards.teaser: President Volodymyr Zelensky requested that the United States provide Ukraine with Patriot missile interceptors to help defend against Russian attacks.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky appealed to President Trump and members of Congress on Wednesday to provide Kyiv with Patriot missile interceptors. The request aims to bolster Ukraine's defense capabilities in its ongoing conflict with Russia.

The plea comes as Ukraine faces intensified Russian attacks on its capital and infrastructure, with Moscow threatening additional strikes against Kyiv following Ukrainian drone and missile strikes on Russian military assets.

cards.headline: Uganda closes border with Congo as Ebola cases reach capital
cards.teaser: Seven confirmed Ebola cases have been reported in Kampala as the country takes preventive measures.
cards.body:
Uganda closed its border with Congo after seven confirmed cases of Ebola were reported in Kampala, the capital. The government took the action as fears rise about the spread of the virus.

Officials said the country has robust disease surveillance systems in place. The cases in the capital represent a concerning development as Ebola reaches Uganda's most populous city.

cards.headline: Israel strikes southern Lebanon after issuing evacuation orders
cards.teaser: The Israeli military declared areas south of the Zahrani River as combat zones.
cards.body:
Israel has launched fresh military strikes in southern Lebanon following evacuation orders to residents. The military has designated areas south of the Zahrani River as "combat zones" as operations begin in the region.

The evacuation orders preceded the attacks, providing residents in targeted areas with notice to leave before the strikes commenced.

cards.headline: Justice Department opens criminal investigation into Trump accuser E. Jean Carroll
cards.body:
The Department of Justice has opened a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll, who accused President Trump of sexual assault, according to multiple reports.

CNN first reported that the investigation focuses on whether Carroll committed perjury during a deposition as part of her two civil cases against Trump. The probe marks a significant escalation in the ongoing legal battles between Carroll and the president.

Carroll won two civil verdicts against Trump in federal court. In May 2023, a jury found Trump liable for sexual abuse and defamation, awarding Carroll $5 million. A separate jury in January 2024 awarded her an additional $83.3 million for defamation after Trump continued to deny her allegations.

The criminal investigation centers on statements Carroll made under oath during depositions related to those civil cases. Perjury charges require prosecutors to prove that a witness knowingly made false statements while under oath about material facts in a case.

Carroll first publicly accused Trump of sexually assaulting her in a Bergdorf Goodman dressing room in the mid-1990s when she published her memoir in 2019. Trump has consistently denied the allegations, claiming he never met Carroll and that she fabricated the story.

The timing of the Justice Department investigation has raised questions given the administration's relationship with the case. Trump previously sued the IRS and has been involved in various legal disputes with federal agencies.

Legal experts note that perjury prosecutions are relatively rare and require a high burden of proof. Prosecutors must demonstrate not only that statements were false, but that the witness knew they were false when making them and that the false statements were material to the proceedings.

The investigation comes as Carroll's legal team has not yet commented publicly on the probe. The Justice Department also has not released additional details about the scope or timeline of the investigation.

Carroll's civil cases against Trump were notable for being among the first successful legal actions brought against him by an accuser. The substantial damage awards reflected the jury's findings that Trump's public statements about Carroll were defamatory and made with malice.

hero.headline: Sixteen pupils killed in Kenya school fire
hero.teaser: Local police confirmed the deaths as search-and-rescue operations continue.
hero.body:
Sixteen pupils died in a school fire in Kenya, according to local police. The incident prompted immediate search-and-rescue operations at the school.

Authorities have not yet confirmed the final number of casualties as operations continue. Police are working to account for all students and assess the full scope of the incident.

cards.headline: Uganda closes border with Congo as Ebola cases reach capital
cards.teaser: Seven confirmed Ebola cases have been reported in Kampala as the country takes preventive measures.
cards.body:
Uganda closed its border with Congo after seven confirmed cases of Ebola were reported in Kampala, the capital. The government took the action as fears rise about the spread of the virus.

Officials said the country has robust disease surveillance systems in place. The cases in the capital represent a concerning development as Ebola reaches Uganda's most populous city.

cards.headline: Pakistan and Afghanistan continue fighting despite Chinese mediation efforts
cards.teaser: Months after Pakistan declared open war, neither country shows signs of backing down.
cards.body:
Pakistan and Afghanistan remain in conflict months after Pakistan declared open war on Afghanistan. Neither side appears ready to back down despite efforts by China to mediate between the two countries.

China has attempted to broker peace between the neighbors but has not achieved a breakthrough. The fighting continues as diplomatic efforts fail to produce a ceasefire or path toward resolution.

cards.headline: Nigel Farage's Reform UK moves from fringe to center of British politics
cards.teaser: The anti-immigrant, populist party has emerged from the margins but faces challenges in winning power.
cards.body:
Nigel Farage's party, Reform UK, has moved from the fringe to become central to British politics. The party's anti-immigrant, populist agenda has helped it gain prominence in the country's political landscape.

Despite its rise, Reform UK faces an uphill climb to win power. The party has successfully shifted from marginal status but must overcome significant obstacles to translate its growing influence into electoral victories.

cards.headline: Australia charges woman who returned from Syria with joining Islamic State
cards.teaser: The woman is among several groups who spent years in a Syrian camp and returned in recent months.
cards.body:
Australia has charged a woman with joining Islamic State after she returned from a Syrian camp where she had been held. The woman was among several groups of women and children who have come back to Australia in recent months after spending years in the camp.

The charges reflect the Australian government's approach to handling citizens who joined or were connected to the terrorist organization. The return of these individuals has prompted legal action as authorities address their involvement with Islamic State.

cards.headline: Jill Biden says she thought Joe Biden was having a stroke during 2024 debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady told CBS News she was frightened by his debate performance against Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Jill Biden told CBS News she was frightened while watching her husband's performance during the 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump. The former first lady said she had never seen Joe Biden perform that way before or since.

In the interview set to air on Sunday, Jill Biden revealed she thought her husband might have suffered a stroke during the debate. She emphasized how unusual and alarming his faltering performance was for her to witness.

cards.headline: Former CIA official charged with stealing $40 million in gold bars
cards.teaser: A former senior CIA official with top secret clearance is accused of stealing hundreds of gold bars from the federal government.
cards.body:
A former senior CIA official with top secret-level clearance has been accused of stealing hundreds of gold bars worth more than $40 million from the federal government. The FBI arrested David Rush after discovering approximately 300 gold bars hidden in his home.

The case represents one of the largest theft allegations against a former U.S. government official in recent years. Federal prosecutors have filed charges related to the stolen precious metals found at his residence.

cards.headline: Trump refiles $10 billion defamation lawsuit against Wall Street Journal
cards.teaser: President Trump filed a revised defamation lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal's publisher over a report on ties to Jeffrey Epstein.
cards.body:
President Trump has filed a revised $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal's publisher over coverage of his alleged connections to Jeffrey Epstein. The new filing comes after a court dismissed his original case on the matter.

The amended lawsuit represents Trump's second attempt to pursue legal action against the newspaper regarding its Epstein-related reporting.

cards.headline: Bronx Zoo euthanizes Happy, elephant known for self-recognition research
cards.teaser: Happy, an elephant who became central to animal rights debates and groundbreaking research, was euthanized at age 55.
cards.body:
The Bronx Zoo euthanized Happy, an elephant who provided researchers with new insight into animal behavior. The 55-year-old elephant taught scientists that elephants can recognize themselves, a significant finding in the study of animal cognition.

Happy became the focus of a closely watched animal rights case in recent years. Her role in research on self-recognition helped advance understanding of elephant intelligence and awareness.

cards.headline: Coffee prices reach $5 as global economic pressures mount
cards.teaser: Coffee at some city center outlets now costs $5, driven by tariffs, climate factors, and shifting consumer tastes.
cards.body:
Some city centre coffee outlets now charge £5 per cup, reflecting a confluence of economic factors reshaping the market. Tariffs, climate conditions, and shifting consumer preferences among younger generations have all contributed to the steep rise in prices.

Coffee farmers have adapted their strategies in response to these market conditions. The surge illustrates broader disruptions affecting global commodity markets and the costs consumers face for everyday goods.

cards.headline: Jill Biden says she thought husband was having stroke during 2024 debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady told CBS News she was frightened by Joe Biden's performance against Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Rewritten Card

Former first lady Jill Biden said she was "frightened" while watching her husband's performance during his 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump. In a CBS News interview set to air Sunday, she revealed she thought Joe Biden might have suffered a stroke, saying she had never seen him perform that way before or since.

Biden's debate appearance became a significant moment in the 2024 campaign, drawing widespread concern from supporters and observers about his performance on stage.

cards.headline: Legal challenge targets UK-funded migrant detention center in France
cards.teaser: A legal bid seeks to block a French detention center backed by the UK under a deal to reduce migrant crossings.
cards.body:
Legal action has been launched against a UK-funded migrant detention center planned for France. The facility is part of a bilateral agreement between the UK and France to reduce migrant crossings of the English Channel.

The Home Office has stated that UK funding is conditional on the site opening. The legal challenge creates uncertainty around the arrangement, which is intended to address migration between the two countries.

hero.headline: Report warns 1.25 million young Britons could be out of work or training by 2031
hero.teaser: One in six people aged 16 to 24 in the UK will not be in work, education or training within five years without intervention, according to a new report.
hero.body:
A report warns that the UK faces a "lost generation" of young people, with 16 to 24-year-olds not in work, education or training projected to reach 1.25 million by 2031. This represents one in six young people in that age group.

The report highlights the risk of rising youth unemployment and disengagement from education without intervention to reverse the trend.

cards.headline: Coffee prices reach $5 at some UK outlets
cards.teaser: A cup of coffee now costs $5 at some city center locations, driven by tariffs, climate factors, changing consumer habits and commodity market dynamics.
cards.body:
Coffee at certain UK city centre outlets now costs £5 per cup, reflecting significant shifts in the global economy. The sharp price increase stems from multiple interconnected factors reshaping the market.

Tariffs, climate conditions and changing consumer preferences among younger generations have all contributed to the rise. Coffee farmers have also become more strategic in their approach to commodity markets, influencing both supply and pricing dynamics across the industry.

cards.headline: Australia sues 3M for $2 billion over firefighting foam chemicals
cards.teaser: The Australian government has filed its largest ever lawsuit against US manufacturer 3M over contamination at defense sites from forever chemicals in firefighting foam.
cards.body:
Australia has launched legal action against US company 3M, seeking A$2 billion in damages over contamination at defence sites caused by chemicals in firefighting foam. This represents the largest lawsuit ever brought by the Australian government.

The chemicals in question are known as "forever chemicals" because they persist in the environment and do not break down naturally.

cards.headline: Google employee charged with insider trading on prediction markets
cards.teaser: A longtime Google worker faces charges in New York for allegedly using internal company data to place bets worth $1.2 million.
cards.body:
Federal prosecutors in New York have charged Google engineer Michele Spagnuolo with insider trading violations. Spagnuolo allegedly used confidential company information about Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign to place bets on Polymarket, a prediction market platform, and profited $1.2 million from the trades.

According to the unsealed complaint, Spagnuolo had access to non-public data about search-related trends that would determine the outcomes of his wagers. He risked over $2.7 million in total bets on the platform, leveraging his insider knowledge to gain an unfair trading advantage before the general public knew the results.

cards.headline: Pork prices in China hit 16-year low
cards.teaser: Pork prices in China have fallen to their lowest level in 16 years, reflecting weak consumer spending and an oversupply of hogs.
cards.body:
Pork prices in China, a key inflation indicator, have reached a 16-year low. The decline stems from both demand and supply factors affecting the Chinese economy.

Weak consumer spending has reduced demand for pork, a staple protein in Chinese diets. At the same time, an oversupply of hogs in the market has pushed prices down further.

cards.headline: Trump administration in talks to fund US drone manufacturers
cards.teaser: The Trump administration is negotiating financial support for American drone companies as Pentagon spending on unmanned aircraft increases.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is discussing financial support for US drone manufacturers as Pentagon spending on unmanned aircraft systems is expected to increase significantly. The potential funding package could reach $54 billion as part of broader military investment priorities.

The announcement has sparked investor interest, with drone company stocks rising following reports of the administration's plans.

cards.headline: China expands factory operations internationally
cards.teaser: Chinese manufacturers are establishing production facilities around the world, raising concerns among competitors about market dominance.
cards.body:
China is exporting its manufacturing infrastructure by building factories in multiple countries. The expansion comes as China maintains a $1.2 trillion trade surplus.

The global spread of Chinese manufacturing operations has triggered unease in competing economies. Some analysts suggest India could benefit from the shifting dynamics in international trade and production.

hero.headline: Australia sues 3M for $2 billion over chemical contamination at defense sites
hero.body:
The Australian government filed a lawsuit against US manufacturing giant 3M over contamination from chemicals in firefighting foam used at defense sites across the country. The case seeks A$2 billion in damages, making it the largest lawsuit ever brought by the Australian government.

The lawsuit centers on so-called forever chemicals in firefighting foam that contaminated military installations. These chemicals, which persist in the environment and do not break down naturally, have been linked to contamination at multiple defense facilities.

3M manufactures a wide range of industrial and consumer products. The company has faced growing scrutiny worldwide over the use of these persistent chemicals in its products, particularly in firefighting foams used by military and emergency services.

The Australian government's legal action represents an escalation in efforts to hold manufacturers accountable for environmental contamination. The chemicals at issue are known as PFAS, or per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, which have been found in water supplies near military bases and firefighting training sites.

The scale of the lawsuit reflects both the extent of contamination across Australian defense sites and the cost of remediation efforts. Forever chemicals earned their nickname because they do not degrade in the environment, leading to long-term contamination issues that can affect groundwater and soil for decades.

3M has faced similar legal challenges in other countries over PFAS contamination. The company previously reached settlements with US water utilities and has set aside billions of dollars to address PFAS-related liabilities. The Australian case adds to mounting global pressure on manufacturers of products containing these chemicals.

The lawsuit seeks compensation for cleanup costs and damages related to the contamination at defense installations. Australian defense sites used firefighting foams containing PFAS for training exercises and emergency response over many years before the full environmental impact of these chemicals became widely understood.

cards.headline: Google engineer charged with insider trading after $1.2 million profit on Polymarket
cards.teaser: A Google engineer faces charges for insider trading after allegedly making $1.2 million on prediction market wagers related to company information.
cards.body:
Federal prosecutors charged Google engineer Michele Spagnuolo with insider trading for allegedly using confidential company information to make approximately $1.2 million in profits on Polymarket, a prediction market platform. The charges center on wagers Spagnuolo placed related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign, which reveals trending search topics.

Prosecutors allege Spagnuolo had advance knowledge of these search trends through his position at Google and risked over $2.7 million total on related bets placed on Polymarket before the information became public.

cards.headline: Rivian sets June 9 for first R2 SUV deliveries
cards.teaser: Electric vehicle maker Rivian announced it will deliver the first R2 SUVs to customers on June 9.
cards.body:
Rivian has announced June 9 as the delivery date for its first R2 SUVs, a major milestone for the electric vehicle manufacturer. CEO RJ Scaringe has described the R2 as potentially the most important product launch in the company's history.

The R2 represents Rivian's expansion beyond its initial R1T truck and R1S SUV offerings, positioning the company to reach a broader market in the competitive electric vehicle segment.

cards.headline: NASA spacecraft captures detailed Mars images during flyby
cards.teaser: A NASA spacecraft captured high-resolution images of Mars, including views of the planet's south pole, during a recent flyby.
cards.body:
NASA's Psyche spacecraft photographed Mars during a flyby on its journey to a distant asteroid. The spacecraft captured detailed images of the red planet, including spectacular views of the Martian south pole.

The flyby provided a unique opportunity to observe Mars from an unusual angle as Psyche continues its mission to study a metal-rich asteroid in the asteroid belt. The spacecraft's imaging system recorded high-resolution views that offer fresh perspectives on Martian surface features. Psyche launched on a multi-year journey to examine an asteroid believed to be the exposed core of an early planet.

cards.headline: Researchers achieve perfect random number generation using quantum mechanics
cards.teaser: Scientists demonstrated true randomness for the first time using quantum computing systems, a breakthrough with implications for encryption and data security.
cards.body:
Researchers successfully generated perfectly random numbers using quantum mechanics, marking the first time true randomness has been achieved experimentally. The breakthrough was published in Nature and represents a significant advance in quantum computing applications.

The ability to create genuinely random numbers has major implications for cryptography and secure communications. Traditional computer systems can only produce pseudo-random numbers based on algorithms, which are theoretically predictable. Quantum randomness relies on the fundamental unpredictability of quantum mechanical processes. The research team's method amplifies naturally occurring quantum randomness to produce numbers that are provably random rather than merely appearing random.

cards.headline: Triomics raises $22 million for cancer-focused AI platform
cards.teaser: Health technology company Triomics secured $22 million in Series B funding to develop AI tools designed specifically for oncology.
cards.body:
Triomics raised $22 million in a Series B funding round led by Battery Ventures. The company develops artificial intelligence systems tailored for cancer treatment centers and oncology practices.

The funding will support expansion of Triomics' AI platform designed to assist cancer centers with clinical decision-making and patient care workflows. The company focuses specifically on oncology applications rather than general medical AI. Specialized AI tools for cancer care represent a growing segment of health technology investment as providers seek ways to manage complex treatment protocols and large volumes of patient data.

cards.headline: Google AI struggles with basic spelling and word recognition
cards.teaser: Google's AI systems have been unable to correctly spell common words, including the company's own name, in recent search results.
cards.body:
Google's artificial intelligence search features have experienced widespread problems with basic word recognition and spelling. Users reported the AI cannot correctly spell words like Google, disregard, stop, and ignore in search responses.

The issues affect Google's AI-powered search summaries, which appear at the top of search results pages. Multiple users documented cases where the AI misspelled simple terms or failed to recognize common words.

hero.headline: Hurricanes rout Canadiens to move within one win of Stanley Cup Final
hero.body:
The Carolina Hurricanes defeated the Montreal Canadiens in Game 4 to take a commanding 3-1 series lead, moving within one victory of reaching the Stanley Cup Final. Goaltender Frederik Andersen recorded 18 saves to earn his third shutout of the postseason.

The Hurricanes now hold an 11-1 record through 12 playoff games this season. Andersen has been a key component of their postseason success, blanking opponents in three of those contests.

Carolina's dominant performance put Montreal in a difficult position, facing elimination in Game 5. The Canadiens will need to win their next game to keep their championship hopes alive and force the series back to Carolina for a sixth contest.

The Hurricanes have demonstrated consistent excellence throughout these playoffs, losing just once in nearly two weeks of postseason play. Their defensive structure has limited opponents while Andersen has provided reliable goaltending when called upon.

Montreal struggled to generate quality scoring chances against Carolina's defense. The Canadiens managed only 18 shots on goal throughout the game, unable to solve Andersen or create sustained offensive pressure.

If Carolina wins Game 5, they will advance to the Stanley Cup Final for the first time since 2006, when they won their only championship in franchise history. The Hurricanes would await the winner of the other conference final series.

The series shifts back to Montreal for Game 5, where the Canadiens will attempt to extend their season and avoid elimination. Carolina will have the opportunity to clinch the series on the road and advance to play for the Stanley Cup.

cards.headline: SEC commissioner defends conference despite Big Ten winning past three national titles
cards.teaser: Greg Sankey said the SEC still stands alone despite the Big Ten's recent dominance in college football playoffs.
cards.body:
SEC commissioner Greg Sankey defended his conference as the nation's best despite recent on-field evidence to the contrary. The Big Ten has won three consecutive national championships and defeated the SEC in all four College Football Playoff matchups over the past three seasons.

Despite the Big Ten's dominance, Sankey maintained that the SEC "stands alone" as college football's premier conference. His remarks came during spring meetings where conference realignment discussions have dominated recent conversations.

cards.headline: Georgia coach suggests SEC could leave NCAA without playoff agreement
cards.teaser: Kirby Smart said the SEC might secede if an agreement on the College Football Playoff cannot be reached.
cards.body:
Georgia head coach Kirby Smart suggested Tuesday that the SEC could break away from the NCAA if negotiators cannot reach an agreement on College Football Playoff terms. His comments came during spring meetings dominated by discussions of conference expansion.

Smart's remarks about a potential SEC departure have raised questions about college football's future structure and the influence of major conferences in shaping it.

cards.headline: Phillies pitcher breaks franchise scoreless innings record from 1911
cards.teaser: Cristopher Sánchez extended his scoreless streak to 44 innings, surpassing Hall of Famer Grover Cleveland Alexander.
cards.body:
Philadelphia Phillies left-hander Cristopher Sánchez set a new franchise record on Wednesday, extending his scoreless innings streak to 44⅔ innings. He surpassed the previous mark held by Hall of Famer Grover Cleveland Alexander, a record that had stood since 1911.

Sánchez's dominant run represents one of the most impressive pitching performances in Phillies history, placing him among baseball's most dominant arms during this stretch.

cards.headline: Former Super Bowl MVP Von Miller seeks return to Broncos
cards.teaser: The veteran pass rusher said he has lobbied Denver coach Sean Payton about rejoining his former team.
cards.body:
Von Miller confirmed Wednesday that he plans to play in the 2026 season and is actively lobbying Denver Broncos coach Sean Payton to bring him back to the franchise. Miller won Super Bowl 50 with Denver and spent the first nine seasons of his career with the team.

The veteran has made his interest in a Broncos reunion clear directly to Payton, hoping to finish his career where it began.

cards.headline: Top transfer portal player withdraws from NBA draft
cards.teaser: Former Iowa State forward Milan Momcilovic will return to college basketball instead of turning professional.
cards.body:
Former Iowa State forward Milan Momcilovic has withdrawn from the NBA draft and will return to college basketball next season, according to his agents. Momcilovic is ranked as the top player available in the transfer portal.

The forward evaluated his professional options before deciding to pursue another year of college basketball. He will now select from among the programs actively recruiting him for next season.

cards.headline: Arizona forward Koa Peat remains in NBA draft
cards.teaser: The projected first-round pick will not return to college basketball.
cards.body:
Arizona forward Koa Peat is staying in the NBA draft, according to sources who spoke with ESPN on Wednesday. The projected first-round pick has decided to forgo his remaining college eligibility and pursue a professional career rather than return to Arizona.

Peat had the option to withdraw from the draft process, but chose instead to continue moving forward toward the upcoming NBA draft.

hero.headline: Multiple Artists Exit DC Freedom 250 Festival Over Trump Administration Ties
hero.body:
Young MC withdrew from the Freedom 250 concert series in Washington on the same day organizers announced the government-sponsored event. The rapper became the second artist to publicly back out of the festival planned for the National Mall.

Morris Day announced earlier the same day that he and the Time would not participate in the event. According to the announcement, artists were never informed about any political involvement with the festival.

The concert series is scheduled to take place on the National Lawn in Washington. A lineup announcement listed performers including Martina McBride, Flo Rida, and Vanilla Ice. Morris Day and the Time appeared in that lineup, but Day denied rumors of their participation.

C+C Music Factory is now weighing its options regarding participation in the festival. The Freedom 250 concert series is part of events marking the country's 250th birthday celebration.

The festival is described as government-sponsored, which appears to be the source of artist concerns about political connections. Young MC's withdrawal came on the announcement day itself, indicating a rapid response once details about the event's backing became public.

The exits represent a public rejection of the festival by performers who say they were not given full information about the event's ties to current political leadership. The timing of the withdrawals suggests coordination or shared concerns among artists about appearing at the government-backed celebration.

cards.headline: Steven Spielberg Says AI Should Not Replace Creative Decisions in Filmmaking
cards.teaser: The director drew a line against artificial intelligence taking over the creative process in Hollywood during a podcast appearance.
cards.body:
Steven Spielberg spoke against using AI in filmmaking during an appearance on Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson's IMO podcast. The director said he thinks AI can be useful for finding solutions to medical issues but opposes it replacing human creativity in film production.

Spielberg stated he does not want AI taking over the creative process in Hollywood. He said Hollywood should never use AI as the final word on anything creative, identifying that boundary as his line on the technology's role in the industry.

cards.headline: ABC News Wins Top Prize at News Emmys for Fourth Consecutive Year
cards.teaser: ABC World News Tonight with David Muir won outstanding live news program for the fourth year running at the 47th annual News Emmys.
cards.body:
ABC News dominated the 47th annual News Emmys, capturing eight awards. ABC World News Tonight with David Muir earned the top prize for outstanding live news program, marking its fourth straight win in the category.

National Geographic finished as a strong runner-up with seven News Emmys. The network's success was bolstered by multiple wins for Trafficked with Mariana van Zeller, bringing it into close contention with ABC News in overall awards at the ceremony.

cards.headline: Student Journalist Criticizes CBS News in Scholarship Acceptance Speech
cards.teaser: Santiago Campos, accepting the Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship, said the recent direction of CBS stains the legacy of Mike Wallace.
cards.body:
Student journalist Santiago Campos criticized CBS News while accepting the Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship at the News Emmys. Campos, a senior at District of Columbia International School in Washington, said the recent direction of the outlet stains the legacy of Mike Wallace.

Former CBS Evening News anchor Scott Pelley presented the scholarship named after the legendary CBS journalist. Campos's remarks during the acceptance speech addressed concerns about the news organization's current editorial approach compared to Wallace's career.

cards.headline: Kanye Label Executive Sues to Identify Person Behind Defamatory Websites
cards.teaser: Larry Jackson filed a lawsuit seeking to unmask an anonymous figure he says is conducting reputational warfare against him.
cards.body:
Larry Jackson, a label boss for Kanye, filed a lawsuit to identify an anonymous person operating defamatory websites. Jackson wants a judge to help unmask the mystery figure targeting him.

Jackson described the campaign as reputational warfare designed to destroy him. The lawsuit seeks court intervention to reveal the identity of the person behind the websites attacking his reputation.

cards.headline: Joan Baez Urges Pop Stars to Speak Out on Politics
cards.teaser: The folk singer discussed her career and ongoing activism, encouraging younger artists to just take that little step into political commentary.
cards.body:
Joan Baez appeared on Julia Louis-Dreyfus's podcast to discuss her career and activism. During the conversation, Baez encouraged pop stars to speak up about politics.

Baez told contemporary musicians to just take that little step into political engagement. The folk singer has maintained activist positions throughout her decades-long career and spoke about continuing that work alongside her music.

cards.headline: Olivia Rodrigo Responds to Criticism Over Recent Outfits
cards.teaser: The singer addressed backlash over her clothing choices, saying women should not be responsible for some guy sexualizing them.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo faced backlash as internet commenters accused her recent clothing choices of both infantilizing and sexualizing the singer. Rodrigo responded to the criticism by addressing the controversy over her outfits.

Rodrigo said women should not be responsible for some guy sexualizing them. Her response addressed accusations about her dress choices that generated debate online about the appropriateness of her fashion selections.

hero.headline: Justice Department opens criminal investigation into Trump accuser E. Jean Carroll
hero.body:
The Department of Justice has opened a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll, who accused President Trump of sexual assault, according to multiple reports.

CNN first reported that the investigation focuses on whether Carroll committed perjury during a deposition as part of her two civil cases against Trump. The probe marks a significant escalation in the ongoing legal battles between Carroll and the president.

Carroll won two civil verdicts against Trump in federal court. In May 2023, a jury found Trump liable for sexual abuse and defamation, awarding Carroll $5 million. A separate jury in January 2024 awarded her an additional $83.3 million for defamation after Trump continued to deny her allegations.

The criminal investigation centers on statements Carroll made under oath during depositions related to those civil cases. Perjury charges require prosecutors to prove that a witness knowingly made false statements while under oath about material facts in a case.

Carroll first publicly accused Trump of sexually assaulting her in a Bergdorf Goodman dressing room in the mid-1990s when she published her memoir in 2019. Trump has consistently denied the allegations, claiming he never met Carroll and that she fabricated the story.

The timing of the Justice Department investigation has raised questions given the administration's relationship with the case. Trump previously sued the IRS and has been involved in various legal disputes with federal agencies.

Legal experts note that perjury prosecutions are relatively rare and require a high burden of proof. Prosecutors must demonstrate not only that statements were false, but that the witness knew they were false when making them and that the false statements were material to the proceedings.

The investigation comes as Carroll's legal team has not yet commented publicly on the probe. The Justice Department also has not released additional details about the scope or timeline of the investigation.

Carroll's civil cases against Trump were notable for being among the first successful legal actions brought against him by an accuser. The substantial damage awards reflected the jury's findings that Trump's public statements about Carroll were defamatory and made with malice.

cards.headline: Former federal judges ask court to review Trump IRS settlement
cards.teaser: A bipartisan group of former judges filed a request to reopen Trump's lawsuit against the IRS over a $1.776 billion settlement fund.
cards.body:
A bipartisan group of former federal judges asked a federal court to reopen President Trump's lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service. The judges argued that the administration circumvented judicial oversight by negotiating a settlement directly with the president rather than proceeding through normal court channels.

The settlement established a $1.776 billion fund for individuals who claim the government wronged them. The former judges contended this approach bypassed standard judicial review procedures.

cards.headline: US military strikes Iranian drone site after intercepting four drones
cards.teaser: American forces shot down four Iranian attack drones and struck a ground control station preparing to launch a fifth drone.
cards.body:
The U.S. military shot down four Iranian attack drones and struck a ground control station in Bandar Abbas after intercepting a fifth drone threat in the Strait of Hormuz. The Iranian military had directed the drones at a commercial ship before U.S. forces intervened, marking the second such confrontation within 48 hours.

These hostilities occur during fragile ceasefire negotiations between the U.S. and Iran aimed at ending their three-month conflict. President Trump has maintained maximum demands in talks while the military continues defensive operations against Iranian drone threats.

cards.headline: Appeals court allows pro-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil to remain free pending Supreme Court appeal
cards.teaser: A three-judge panel ruled that Mahmoud Khalil can stay out of custody while he petitions the Supreme Court in his case against the Trump administration.
cards.body:
A federal appeals court panel allowed pro-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil to remain free while he pursues his case against the Trump administration at the Supreme Court. The 3rd Circuit judges put the circuit court's previous ruling on hold to permit Khalil to prepare his petition to the nation's highest court.

The three-judge panel included Stephanos Bibas, appointed by President Trump; Arianna Freeman, appointed by former President Joe Biden; and Thomas Hardiman, appointed by former President George W. Bush.

cards.headline: Senator Andy Kim responds to Homeland Security chief over detention facility protest
cards.teaser: Democratic Senator Andy Kim pushed back after Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin criticized him for attending a protest at a New Jersey migrant detention facility.
cards.body:
Democratic Sen. Andy Kim of New Jersey defended his attendance at a protest outside a migrant detention facility after Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin criticized him during a White House Cabinet meeting. Mullin referenced Kim being hit with pepper ball spray at the demonstration.

Kim countered that the incident was never about him personally, emphasizing that his focus remained on the broader issues at the ICE facility where demonstrators had gathered.

cards.headline: Senate Republican leaders endorse Ken Paxton after Texas primary
cards.teaser: Senate Majority Leader John Thune endorsed Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton following his $130 million primary victory over Senator John Cornyn.
cards.body:
Senate Republican leaders are moving to repair their relationship with Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton following a contentious primary battle. Senate Majority Leader John Thune spoke with Paxton by phone and subsequently endorsed him on a radio program.

The effort signals to major donors that Republican hopes for maintaining their Senate majority depend heavily on success in Texas. The primary race between Paxton and Sen. John Cornyn was expensive and divisive, and GOP leadership is now focused on uniting the party ahead of the general election.

cards.headline: Ukrainian President Zelensky asks Trump and Congress for Patriot missile interceptors
cards.teaser: President Volodymyr Zelensky requested that the United States provide Ukraine with Patriot missile interceptors to help defend against Russian attacks.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky appealed to President Trump and members of Congress on Wednesday to provide Kyiv with Patriot missile interceptors. The request aims to bolster Ukraine's defense capabilities in its ongoing conflict with Russia.

The plea comes as Ukraine faces intensified Russian attacks on its capital and infrastructure, with Moscow threatening additional strikes against Kyiv following Ukrainian drone and missile strikes on Russian military assets.
